x: 880 yards (Seniors): 1 Wilson (B.); 2 Chard (W.M.T.); 3 Edwards (S.); 4 Hicks (S.); 5 Spencer (M.P.).

The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of a dozen, including our own trio, Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop on the other.
Jack's progress was a treat to watch, for from 6 miles he slowly went through to pass Keily, Hicks, Heywood, our second claim member Bill Bird, running a 'blinder', and was soon lying about 15th.

Steady as the pace was, the leaders were gradually dropping all sorts of big noises, but not our marathon novice Len, who had the "audacity" to lead at 13 miles and refused to drop a yard until 17 miles, when he lay 6th in the company of Hicks, Keily, Smith and Co.

Our Jim got stuck into the battle with his usual spirit but had to give way to that promising Valley star, Hicks. John Moore showed that he was back on form once again, pegging back two more positions on the fourth leg to place us 4th at halfway, only 68secs behind the leaders.

Clive Shippen again took the Dale Hill leg, but it was soon obvious that he was not in his best condition and slowly Hicks of TVH gained to eventually pass him and give the Valley a 180 yds lead over us.

Peter set off shoulder to shoulder with Hicks of Aldershot, 42secs behind the leaders. Showing impressive form, the young pair forged their way through the string of teams ahead, passing the front runner in the final stretch.
